subject: Decision Making
title: Kahneman and Tversky Meet
description: A quick, practical guide to Kahneman and Tversky Meet.

hook.text: In 1969, two Israeli psychologists met at a seminar. Their partnership rewrote everything we know about decisions.

buildup.text: Kahneman was cautious and self-doubting. Tversky was bold and charismatic. Opposites who thought as one mind.

discovery.text: They discovered that humans make systematic errors in judgment. Not random mistakes but predictable, repeatable biases.

twist.text: Their work was so intertwined they flipped a coin to decide whose name went first on each paper.

climax.text: Kahneman won the Nobel in 2002. Tversky had died in 1996. The Prize cannot be awarded posthumously.

punchline.text: Two minds, one revolution. They proved human bias is predictable.

quiz.question: What did Kahneman and Tversky discover?
options: Humans make systematic, predictable errors in judgment
